title: Lost Your Job? Don’t Update Your Resume Until You Do This First
description:
Lost your job and panicking about your resume? Pause. Most job seekers make the same mistake — rushing to update their resume while stressed, forgetting their biggest wins, and turning a simple update into an overwhelming spiral.

Before you touch your resume, start here.

Create a simple “brag bank” — a messy document where you collect your wins, results, problems solved, metrics, and proof. Hiring managers don’t hire responsibilities. They hire evidence you can solve their problems.

In this video, I’ll show you:
• What to do immediately after a job loss
• Why updating your resume too soon backfires
• A simple system to capture your career wins
• How to use AI to turn your proof into strong resume bullets

This is how you stop scrambling and start job searching strategically.

transcript: If you get laid off, do this first before you even touch your resume. When something unexpected happens, your brain panics. You forget your wins, and your resume suddenly feels impossible, and a simple update turns into an all-day spiral. That's a mistake almost everyone makes. The first thing you need is not a resume, it's a brag bank. This is not fancy, it's not formatted, it's just a messy document where you dump your proof. Project you finished, problems you solved, time or money you saved, a thank you email, a Slack message that says you saved us. Basically, receipts. Because hiring managers don't hire responsibilities, they hire proof. And if you wait until you're stressed to remember your proof, you forget half of it. Do this instead. Open a plain doc and create three sections: wins and results, problems you solved, and proof. And then let AI help you. You paste that brag bank into AI with the job description and ask it to polish. That's how you stop scrambling, that's how you stay layoff-ready. Check out my long-form video, and don't forget to follow.
